$a \bmod b$ is read “a mod b” and is the remainder of dividing $a$ by $b$.

Why it is correct: every common divisor of $a$ and $b$ also divides the remainder, because $r = a - q\,b$. So $\gcd(a, b) = \gcd(b, r)$, and the problem keeps getting smaller without changing the answer.

Why it terminates: the remainder is always smaller than $b$, so $b$ drops on every pass, and a natural number cannot drop for ever. It reaches 0, and then the gcd is whatever is in $a$.

No improvement in the computer makes up for choosing the algorithm badly. The question of which problems have fast algorithms and which do not is one of the great open mysteries of mathematics, and it is told in [[av-complejidad]].
Cuando buscas un contacto en el móvil, e: When you look up a contact on your phone, it does not scan the thousand names one by one: they are sorted and it does a binary search. Photos are compressed with algorithms based on the waves of [[av-fourier]], and every secure internet connection runs Euclid's algorithm with numbers of hundreds of digits. La palabra <em>algoritmo</em> es el nomb: The word algorithm is a person's name. Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi was a Persian mathematician who worked at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad around the year 820. He wrote a book on how to calculate with the Indian numerals, the ones with zero, which was translated into Latin under the title Algoritmi de numero Indorum: “Al-Khwarizmi on the numbers of the Indians”. Europeans ended up calling the calculation procedures of that book “algorithms”. From another of his books, al-jabr, comes the word algebra.

Un <strong>algoritmo</strong> es una rec: An algorithm is a recipe so precise that it can be followed by somebody — or something — that does not understand what it is doing. The long division you learned at primary school is an algorithm: you follow it step by step without thinking and it always gives the quotient. [[al-gauss|Gaussian]] elimination for solving systems is too. And so is the one your phone uses to find the shortest route.
Un algoritmo cuadrático tarda cuatro vec: A quadratic algorithm takes four times as long with twice the data, on any machine. What matters is how the time grows, not how long it takes today.
Un algoritmo escrito en castellano no lo: An algorithm written in plain words is not run by anybody; you need a language, and a language is a text that another program translates. In [[len-taller|the workshop of the machines and languages block]] a whole one — seven keywords — is built, with its interpreter and its compiler, and you can write in it inside the page itself.
